examples: 한국 생활에 조금 익숙해졌어요.
I have gotten a little used to life in Korea.
생활 focuses on everyday rhythm, not one event.
nuance: 생활 is the life you live day to day: home, school, work, habits, and routine.
mistakes: Do not use 인생 for an ordinary daily routine; 인생 is life as a whole.

examples: 인생에서 중요한 순간이에요.
It is an important moment in life.
인생 sounds bigger than everyday 생활.
nuance: 인생 usually looks at a person's life as a whole story.
mistakes: For daily living in Korea, 한국 생활 is more natural than 한국 인생.

usage: restaurant meal instead of home food
examples: 오늘은 집에서 안 먹고 외식할 거예요.
Today I will eat out instead of eating at home.
외식 contrasts with eating at home.
nuance: 외식 literally points to eating outside the home.
mistakes: Do not use 식당 as the action; 식당 is the place, 외식 is the activity.

examples: 이번 휴가는 국내 여행을 할 거예요.
This vacation I will travel domestically.
국내 contrasts with 해외 or 외국.
nuance: 국내 means inside one country, often Korea in a Korean context.
mistakes: Do not confuse 국내 with 나라. 나라 is a country; 국내 is inside the country.

examples: 요즘은 스마트폰 시대예요.
These days it is the smartphone era.
시대 frames a broad period, not one clock time.
nuance: 시대 uses 시 as time on a large historical or social scale.
mistakes: For appointment time, use 시간 or 시, not 시대.

usage: to do at the same time
examples: 두 일을 동시에 하기 어려워요.
It is hard to do two things at the same time.
동시에 marks overlap in time.
nuance: 동시에 combines same and time: two things happening together.
mistakes: Do not use 동안 for 'at the same time'; 동안 means during or for a duration.

examples: 퇴근 후에는 개인 시간이 필요해요.
After work, I need personal time.
개인 contrasts with group or company.
nuance: 개인 uses 인 as person and points to one person rather than a group.
mistakes: 개인 is not the same as 사람; 사람 is a person, 개인 is an individual.

examples: 외국인도 이 앱으로 한국어를 공부할 수 있어요.
Foreigners can also study Korean with this app.
외국인 is person-from-outside-country.
nuance: 외국인 combines outside-country and person.
mistakes: 한국 사람 and 한국인 both work, but 외국인 is the normal compact word for a foreign person.

examples: 그 카페는 학생들 사이에서 인기가 많아요.
That cafe is popular among students.
인기 is attention or favor from people.
nuance: 인기 is about how many people like, watch, buy, or talk about something.
mistakes: Use 인기가 많아요, not 인기가 커요, for ordinary popularity.

examples: 저는 부산에 있는 대학교에 다녀요.
I attend a university in Busan.
대학교 uses 대 for big and 교 for school.
nuance: 대학교 is the full word for university; 대학 is the shorter common form.
mistakes: Do not translate every college as 학교; 대학교 is the specific school level.

examples: 이 방은 최대 네 명까지 들어갈 수 있어요.
This room can hold up to four people.
최대 marks the biggest allowed amount.
nuance: 최대 means the greatest size, number, or limit.
mistakes: 최대 is a limit word; for 'most people', 대부분 is usually more natural.

examples: 글자가 작으면 화면을 확대해 보세요.
If the letters are small, try enlarging the screen.
확대 is making the scale bigger.
nuance: 확대 uses 대 as big: the thing becomes larger in size or scope.
mistakes: 확대 is not the same as 대단하다; 대단하다 praises something as impressive.

examples: 여행에는 소형 가방이 편해요.
A small bag is convenient for travel.
소형 describes a small category or model.
nuance: 소형 is common on products, housing, cars, and devices when the type is small.
mistakes: For a normal adjective before a noun, 작은 is often simpler than 소형.

examples: 최소 세 시간은 걸릴 것 같아요.
I think it will take at least three hours.
최소 marks the lower bound.
nuance: 최소 is the smallest limit or amount in a range.
mistakes: Do not use 최소 for physically small objects; use 작은 or 소형.

usage: making the size or scope smaller
examples: 행사 규모가 축소됐어요.
The event scale was reduced.
축소 is the opposite direction from 확대.
nuance: 축소 uses 소 as small and points to making something smaller.
mistakes: 축소 is formal; in daily speech 줄이다 is often easier.

examples: 화재가 나면 119에 전화하세요.
If there is a fire, call 119.
화재 is the formal emergency word for fire.
nuance: 화재 is the incident word used in news, signs, insurance, and safety notices.
mistakes: 불 is the simple word for fire; 화재 is a fire accident.

examples: 문 옆에 소화기가 있어요.
There is a fire extinguisher next to the door.
소화기 is a safety item for putting out fire.
nuance: 소화기 contains 화 for fire, not 화 for speech or Tuesday.
mistakes: Do not confuse this with 소화제, digestive medicine.

examples: 이번 달 전기 요금이 많이 나왔어요.
This month's electricity bill was high.
전기 is the basic electricity word.
nuance: 전기 is useful for bills, appliances, and home problems.
mistakes: 전화 is a phone call; 전기 is electricity.

examples: 학교 정문 앞에서 만나요.
Let's meet in front of the school main gate.
정문 is the main entrance gate.
nuance: 정문 is the main gate, while 후문 is a back gate.
mistakes: 문 alone is a door; 정문 is specifically the main gate or entrance.

examples: 이 근처에 김밥 전문점이 있어요.
There is a gimbap specialty shop nearby.
전문점 is a shop specializing in one thing.
nuance: 전문점 uses 문 in 전문, a learned word meaning specialized field or expertise.
mistakes: Do not use 전문점 for any store; it suggests a store focused on one category.

examples: 이 문법은 예문으로 익히면 쉬워요.
This grammar is easier if you learn it through examples.
문법 points to language rules.
nuance: 문법 combines writing/language and law/rule.
mistakes: 문법 is rules; 문장 is a sentence.

examples: 어제 뉴스에서 그 사건을 봤어요.
I saw that incident on the news yesterday.
사건 is a notable thing that happened.
nuance: 사건 is often bigger or more newsworthy than 일.
mistakes: 사고 is an accident; 사건 can be any notable case or incident.

examples: 처음 만나면 먼저 인사를 해요.
When you meet someone for the first time, you greet them first.
인사 is a social action between people.
nuance: 인사 can mean greeting, personnel, or polite acknowledgement by context.
mistakes: 인사하다 is the verb; 인사 is the noun.

examples: 약속 장소를 다시 확인해 주세요.
Please check the meeting place again.
장소 is a general place word.
nuance: 장소 is broader and more formal than 데 or 곳.
mistakes: 시장 is a specific place; 장소 is the category word place/location.

examples: 비가 와서 실내에서 운동했어요.
It rained, so I exercised indoors.
실내 contrasts with 야외.
nuance: 실내 combines room and inside.
mistakes: 실내 is indoors; 방 is one room.

examples: 방이 추운데 난방이 안 돼요.
The room is cold, but the heating is not working.
난방 is heating for a room or building.
nuance: 난방 is common in housing, hotel, and maintenance contexts.
mistakes: Do not confuse 난방 with 방. 방 is a room; 난방 is heating.

examples: 상의는 흰색으로 입을게요.
I will wear a white top.
상의 is clothing for the upper body.
nuance: 상의 uses 상 for upper and contrasts with 하의.
mistakes: 상의 can also mean consultation in another Hanja word; here it is upper clothing.

examples: 세 명 이상이면 예약해야 해요.
If it is three or more people, you need a reservation.
이상 includes the number named.
nuance: 이상 uses 상 as above and includes the reference point.
mistakes: 이상하다 is a different word meaning strange.

examples: 매일 들으면 듣기 실력이 향상돼요.
If you listen every day, your listening skill improves.
향상 carries an upward-progress feeling.
nuance: 향상 is improvement in ability, quality, or level.
mistakes: 향상 is a noun; 향상되다 is the verb to improve.

examples: 하의는 검은색으로 입을게요.
I will wear black bottoms.
하의 is clothing for the lower body.
nuance: 하의 uses 하 as lower and contrasts with 상의.
mistakes: Do not confuse 하의 with 하이. It is a clothing noun.

examples: 오천 원 이하 메뉴가 있어요?
Do you have menu items that are 5,000 won or less?
이하 includes the number named.
nuance: 이하 uses 하 as below and includes the reference point.
mistakes: 이하 is the opposite of 이상 in ranges.

examples: 주말에 시내에 갈 거예요.
I am going downtown this weekend.
시내 points to inside the city.
nuance: 시내 is the inside/central part of a city.
mistakes: Do not confuse 시내 with 시대; 시내 is a place, 시대 is an era.

examples: 집 앞에서 공사를 하고 있어요.
They are doing construction in front of my home.
공사 is work that builds or repairs.
nuance: 공사 uses 공 for work/building, not 공 for empty sky.
mistakes: 회사 is a company; 공사 is construction work.

examples: 그 도시는 큰 공장이 많아요.
That city has many large factories.
공장 is a place for manufacturing.
nuance: 공장 combines work/building and place.
mistakes: Do not confuse 공장 with 공항. 공항 is airport and uses a different 공.

examples: 인공 지능 앱을 써 봤어요.
I tried an artificial intelligence app.
인공 means made by people, not natural.
nuance: 인공 contains 공 for making or work; it means human-made.
mistakes: Do not place 인공 under 공(空); this is 공(工), making/work.

english: movement; moving from one place to another
examples: 공항까지 이동 시간이 얼마나 걸려요?
How long does the travel time to the airport take?
이동 is movement between places.
nuance: 이동 is a formal, useful word for movement, travel, or transfer.
mistakes: 이동 is not simply 걷다; it covers movement by any method.

examples: 저는 동물을 좋아해요.
I like animals.
동물 uses 동 for movement and 물 for thing.
nuance: 동물 literally points to a living/moving thing.
mistakes: For a pet, 반려동물 sounds warmer and more modern than 애완동물.

examples: 입사 전에 신체 검사를 받아야 해요.
Before joining the company, I have to get a physical exam.
신체 is more formal than 몸.
nuance: 신체 is a formal body word used in health, rules, and documents.
mistakes: In casual speech 몸 is simpler; 신체 is more formal.

examples: 전체 내용을 한 번에 이해하기 어려워요.
It is hard to understand the whole content at once.
전체 means the whole, not one part.
nuance: 전체 combines all/complete with body/form: the whole body of something.
mistakes: 전부 is a casual all/everything word; 전체 sounds more structural.

examples: 한복 체험을 해 봤어요.
I tried a hanbok experience.
체험 is experience through doing or trying.
nuance: 체험 is common in tourism, classes, and activity programs.
mistakes: 경험 is experience in general; 체험 is more hands-on.

examples: 이 이야기는 가족을 중심으로 전개돼요.
This story develops around a family.
중심 is the center or focus.
nuance: 중심 combines middle and heart, so it can mean physical center or main focus.
mistakes: 중간 is middle position; 중심 is center or focus.

examples: 비가 오니까 길에서 조심하세요.
It is raining, so be careful on the road.
조심 is care/caution, often used as a warning.
nuance: 조심 is the noun-like root behind 조심하다 and 조심하세요.
mistakes: 조심 is not an emotion noun like 관심; it is caution in action.

examples: 그 광고는 사람의 심리를 잘 이용해요.
That ad uses people's psychology well.
심리 is about the mind and inner response.
nuance: 심리 is a learned word for mental state, psychology, or inner motivation.
mistakes: 마음 is the everyday heart/mind word; 심리 is more analytical.

examples: 이 박물관은 오늘 무료예요.
This museum is free today.
무료 means no fee is charged.
nuance: 무료 contains 료 as fee; it means the fee is zero.
mistakes: 공짜 is casual; 무료 is clearer in signs, apps, and official notices.

examples: 김치찌개 재료를 샀어요.
I bought ingredients for kimchi stew.
재료 is what you use to make food or a product.
nuance: 재료 is material or ingredient, useful in cooking and making things.
mistakes: Do not confuse 재료 with 요리. 요리 is cooking or a dish; 재료 is the ingredient.

examples: 한국에 온 지 삼 개월 됐어요.
It has been three months since I came to Korea.
개월 counts a length of months.
nuance: 개월 counts months as a duration, unlike 월요일 or 이번 달.
mistakes: Use 세 달 in casual speech too; 개월 is a compact Sino-Korean counter.

examples: 일주일에 두 번 한국어를 공부해요.
I study Korean twice a week.
일주일 is one week as a time unit.
nuance: 일주일 is the everyday word for one week.
mistakes: Do not use 주말 for one week; 주말 means weekend.
